questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Burundi?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Burundi on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Burundi article.

questions.proof: It is bordered by Rwanda to the north, Tanzania to the east and south and the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the west.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Burundi?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Burundi article.

questions.proof: The official languages of Burundi are Kirundi, Swahili, French and English.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It is linked from Lake _____ to its headwaters by the Ruvyironza River.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Lake”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Burundi article, under the heading “Geography”.

questions.proof: It is linked from Lake Victoria to its headwaters by the Ruvyironza River.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “In 1962, Burundi gained independence from _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “independence”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Burundi article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: In 1962, Burundi gained independence from Belgium.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Both were formed in _____ to keep wildlife populations.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Burundi article, under the heading “Geography”.

questions.proof: Both were formed in 1982 to keep wildlife populations.
